message: File the zero-headroom related ceiling measured while filing this session's findings

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value:
## The two declarations

Both live in the same registry and both descend from pm-q6n8sj, which correctly identified that `related` was the largest edge population and the only unbounded one.

```
related-to-ceiling         edges-related               ceiling 6053   block   owner pm-q6n8sj
  negative_control: 6053 pass / 6054 fail
  authorization_decision: pm-4jqm

semantic-edge-share-floor  semantic-edge-share-permille  floor 79     block   owner pm-q6n8sj
  negative_control: 79 pass / 78 fail
```

The share floor is the one that expresses the intent. It fails exactly when the fraction of traversable edges falls, which is the dilution pm-q6n8sj set out to prevent. It is indifferent to how large the graph gets, which is the correct indifference.

The raw ceiling is pinned to the count observed when it was declared. Its negative control states that one more associative row than existed at that instant is a failure.

## What that means in practice

Filing four findings this session, each with the associative sibling context an item is supposed to carry, took `edges-related` from 6,053 to 6,063. Both `graph-composition` and `tracker-context-quality` went to `verdict: block`.

Semantic share over the same edit went from 81.0 to 81.2 permille against a floor of 79. The edit the raw ceiling refused was an edit that improved the quantity the project says it cares about.

Retyping those ten rows to `implements`, `verifies` and `discovered_from` cleared both gates and moved semantic edges from 836 to 849 and share to 70.0 permille of total edges by the audit's own basis. That outcome is good, and it is the outcome the share floor would have produced on its own. The raw ceiling contributed nothing except the failure.

## Why the incentive is wrong, not just inconvenient

With the ceiling at zero headroom, an agent recording two genuinely-associated items has three options: leave the relation unrecorded, spell it as a semantic kind it does not deserve, or fail the build. The second is the cheapest and the most damaging, and it is the precise failure mode the operating rules already warn about — a cue names a relation's kind and object, never its subject, so lexical promotion of associative links to semantic ones has already been measured at precision zero out of eight.

A bound whose cheapest compliant response is mislabelling is worse than no bound.

## Addition safety by kind, as currently declared

| kind | bound | adding an edge |
|---|---|---|
| implements | floor 2591 | always safe |
| discovered_from | floor 474 | always safe |
| verifies | floor 245 | always safe |
| supersedes | floor 84 | always safe |
| blocked_by | none declared | safe |
| related | ceiling 6053 | fails at any addition |
| blocks | ceiling 243 | fails at any addition |

Only the two ceiling-bounded kinds are addition-unsafe, and both are pinned to their observation. `blocks` has an independent and deliberate rationale on pm-c90tfh — fabricated ordering edges are the specific harm there — so the two cases should be dispositioned separately rather than as one policy.

## Boundary

This is not a request to raise the number. Raising a pinned ratchet by hand is the erosion these declarations exist to catch. The repair is to enforce composition and demote the raw count to reporting.

message: Record the two overlapping declarations and the observed sequence

patch.value: The raw related-edge ceiling is pinned to the observed count, so one legitimate associative link fails enforcement even when semantic composition improves. Govern associative growth by dilution ratio or explicit justified headroom, retain a negative control, and make addition-safe edge guidance discoverable before mutation.
